item.title: Anthropic Asks Claude Users to Share Voice Recordings for AI Training With a New Opt-In Setting (2026)
item.description:
Anthropic has started asking Claude users to share their voice conversations so the company can use them to train and improve its AI models. The request appears as a prompt when people use Claude's voice features, and Anthropic has added a matching option to Claude's Privacy settings. Sharing is optional, and the setting is turned off by default in the interface seen so far.

The prompt reads "Allow us to use your voice data to improve our AI models." It adds that "audio recordings and voice chat data help improve how Anthropic AI models understand and respond to speech," and tells users they can turn the option off or delete the data at any time in settings. Users can respond with either Allow or Not now.

Claude Voice Training Uses a Separate Privacy Toggle

Voice data has its own control. Anthropic already offers an option to let it use regular chats and Claude Code sessions for model training, and the new voice setting is independent of that choice.

Two combinations are possible as a result. A user can allow training on voice conversations while keeping regular chats and coding sessions excluded, or share text chats while keeping voice recordings out of training.

Inside Settings > Privacy, the new option is labeled "Allow us to use your voice data." Anthropic's description in the setting reads: "For approved sessions, allow the use of your audio recordings and voice chat data to improve Anthropic AI models."

Anthropic says users can switch the option off later and delete their voice data from settings if they change their mind.

The voice request follows other recent Claude changes, including the launch of the Claude Marketplace with 2,000 connectors in late September.

Claude users who want to check or change the setting can do so in a few steps:

  1. Open Claude and go to Settings.
  2. Select Privacy.
  3. Find the option labeled "Allow us to use your voice data."
  4. Leave it off to keep voice recordings out of training, or turn it on to share audio from approved sessions.
  5. Check the separate training option for chats and Claude Code sessions, since changing the voice toggle does not affect it.

Users who tap Allow in the voice prompt by mistake can reverse the decision with the same toggle and delete the voice data from settings.

The prompt and the setting text do not state how long approved voice recordings are kept, and Anthropic has not said whether the request is shown to all Claude users or only to some accounts so far.

item.title: PEGI Rates GTA 6 18 Over Decapitation, Drug Use, and Sexual Content in a Since-Deleted Listing (2026)
item.description:
Grand Theft Auto 6 has received an 18 rating from PEGI, the European age rating organization, and the listing described the game's adult content in unusual detail before it was removed from PEGI's website.

The rating summary said Rockstar's game "features strong graphic violence, strong sexual themes, and use of illegal drugs," and the content notes revealed specific gaming mechanics that Rockstar has not detailed itself. GTA 6 launches on consoles on November 19.

The PEGI rating adds to the age ratings already published for GTA 6, including the Mature rating covered in GTA 6's M rating in Australia. PEGI went further than the other boards in describing what players can actually do.

What the Deleted PEGI Listing Says About GTA 6

On violence, PEGI wrote that "violence is bloody with a high degree of realism, with certain weapons being able to cause greater damage such as detailed decapitation and dismemberment."

Earlier Grand Theft Auto games mostly showed violence through blood pools, bullet wound decals, and physics-driven animations, so dismemberment is a clear change for the series.

Drug use is described as "frequent and prominent." According to PEGI, players can use illegal drugs directly from their inventory, and the listing gave one example: cocaine can be carried by the player and snorted from their hand at any time. The listing does not say whether drug use has gameplay effects.

The sexual content notes are the most specific. PEGI said GTA 6 includes "scenes of intercourse and occasional scenes of sexual fetishes." The listing also describes a strip club where players can pay for private dances and move their hands onto the dancers' bodies.

Rockstar's August gameplay reveal showed that protagonists Jason and Lucia can be played as a couple in a long-term relationship, although the relationship does not have to be romantic. The PEGI listing does not say how the intercourse scenes connect to that storyline.

GTA 6 Rating and Release Details

The PEGI 18 rating means the game is intended for adults only in countries that use the PEGI system. Parents who manage console accounts for younger players can use the PEGI 18 label to set age restrictions before the November 19 launch.

GTA 6 is coming to consoles first. A PC release date has not been announced.

PEGI has not explained why the GTA 6 listing was removed from its website, and Rockstar has not commented on the content details the listing revealed.

item.title: OpenAI Will Test Visual Ads in ChatGPT During Image Generation in the US Later This Month (2026)
item.description:
OpenAI is introducing a visual ad format in ChatGPT and will test it first while users generate images, the company announced on October 5, 2026. Testing begins later in October in the United States with an initial group of advertisers.

OpenAI says the new ads use pictures to show product inspiration, how a product is used, or the experiences a service offers. The ads will be clearly labeled and kept separate from the image ChatGPT is creating. The company also repeats its position that advertising does not influence the answers ChatGPT provides.

ChatGPT now reaches 1.2 billion people each week, according to OpenAI, which describes advertising as a way to serve a much larger market than subscriptions alone.

How Visual Ads Will Appear During ChatGPT Image Generation

Image generation is the only surface named for the test. Example screenshots published by OpenAI show ChatGPT on mobile displaying a grocery brand's product images with a "Learn more" button while an image request is processed.

OpenAI says its placement guardrails assess whether a conversation is appropriate for advertising and are meant to keep ads out of emotionally vulnerable, sensitive, or otherwise unsuitable contexts.

Automated review, human oversight, and ongoing monitoring are used to find policy violations. Qualifying advertisers can also use a new Negative Phrases option to exclude placements that conflict with their own brand policies.

The announcement does not say which ChatGPT plans will see the visual ads during the US test. Users who generate images in ChatGPT should watch for the ad label, which OpenAI says separates sponsored content from the generated image.

New Measurement Tools and Partners for ChatGPT Ads

The other half of the update targets advertisers. OpenAI is adding integrations with Hightouch, Tealium, and LiveRamp so businesses can send conversion data from their existing systems to ChatGPT Ads.

Supported attribution partners now include AppsFlyer, Adjust, Branch, Kochava, Singular, Northbeam, Triple Whale, DV Rockerbox, Airbridge, and Tenjin.

Incrementality testing is at an early stage. OpenAI is working with Haus, Measured, and WorkMagic on geo-based experiments that measure the causal impact of ChatGPT Ads.

Early partner figures shared by the company include a 15.3% lower attributed cost per acquisition for WeightWatchers compared with its blended paid search benchmark.

DoubleVerify and Integral Ad Science are running brand suitability pilots in a controlled testing environment. OpenAI says the two companies will evaluate how its safeguards work without accessing private user conversations.

OpenAI has not said when the visual format will expand beyond image generation or reach markets outside the United States. The company says it will keep adding ad formats and capabilities, and businesses of all sizes can already sign up for ChatGPT Ads through its advertising portal.

item.title: Microsoft Confirms Windows 11 KB5124010 Crashes Games and Apps That Use Dolby Digital Audio (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft has confirmed that KB5124010, the September 22, 2026 preview update for Windows 11, can crash some games, media players, and productivity applications that rely on AC-3 (Dolby Digital) audio decoding. The company added the known issue to the Windows release health dashboard on October 2 and says a fix will ship in a future Windows update.

The problem affects Windows 11 versions 26H2, 25H2, and 24H2. Windows Server is not on the list of affected platforms. Microsoft names OS Build 26300.9550 as the originating update.

How the KB5124010 Dolby Digital Bug Affects Applications

According to Microsoft, the symptoms depend on what the affected program is doing at the time. Some applications fail to launch or close without warning. Others run normally until a feature that needs AC-3 decoding is used, such as playing music, and then shut down.

The component behind the crashes is mostly used by legacy software that still relies on the audio decoding built into Windows, Microsoft says. Modern applications often ship their own decoding components, even when they support the older AC-3 codec, and those programs should not run into the problem. Microsoft has not published a list of affected games or applications.

KB5124010 is an optional preview, so most systems only get it when the user selects "Download and install" in Windows Update. Devices running Windows 11 version 24H2 with the "Get the latest updates as soon as they're available" option turned on are the exception, because they receive the update automatically.

The AC-3 crash adds to a run of audio problems after September's releases. Microsoft also lists a mitigated issue where some USB Audio Class 1.0 devices fail to start, show a Code 10 error in Device Manager, or produce no sound after users install the Windows 11 version 26H2 enablement package.

What Windows 11 Users Can Do Until Microsoft Ships a Fix

Microsoft has not provided a workaround or a Known Issue Rollback for the Dolby Digital crashes. Users who rely on older games or media players can avoid the problem by staying off the optional preview for now:

  1. Open Settings and select Windows Update.
  2. Skip the "Download and install" link for KB5124010 while it is listed as an optional update.
  3. Turn off "Get the latest updates as soon as they're available" on Windows 11 version 24H2 devices, since that setting installs the preview automatically.
  4. Check Update history for KB5124010 if a legacy application starts closing unexpectedly when it plays audio.

Skipping the preview also delays the other changes it includes until they arrive in a regular monthly update. The trade-off mainly matters for systems that run older software with Dolby Digital audio.

Microsoft says it is working on a resolution for a future Windows update but has not given a release date or said whether the fix will arrive in the October Patch Tuesday release.

item.title: Google Docs Adds Native Markdown File Editing, With Rendered .md Previews in Google Drive (2026)
item.description:
Google is rolling out native Markdown support in Google Docs, letting users view, edit, and collaborate on .md and .markdown files without converting them to the Docs format, according to an October 5, 2026 post on the Google Workspace Updates blog.

Google Drive also gains rendered previews for Markdown files. The feature is available to all Google Workspace customers and to users with personal Google accounts.

The rollout started on October 5 for both Rapid Release and Scheduled Release domains. Google says it can take up to 15 days for the feature to become visible on every account.

How Markdown Support Works in Google Docs and Drive

Until now, Markdown files had to be imported and converted into a Google Doc. Google acknowledges that the conversion often altered formatting, stripped comments, and fragmented files.

With native support, a .md file opens directly in Docs and keeps its file type after editing. Real-time editing and commenting still work, and collaborators do not need to write raw Markdown syntax.

Google describes Markdown as a standard text format widely used by large language models to preserve structured content such as tables, headers, and bulleted lists, and says the change lets both people and AI agents work on the same files without manual conversions.

Drive now renders Markdown as formatted documents with clickable links and structured tables, so users can read a file's layout before opening it in Docs. Google calls the result fully formatted documents.

Markdown support has been a frequent request in Google's own support forums and on Reddit. Proton Docs, a competing editor, has handled Markdown files for more than two years.

How to Open Markdown Files in Google Docs

Google says there is no admin control and no end user setting for the feature. Markdown editing appears automatically once the rollout reaches an account. To check whether it is active:

  1. Upload a .md or .markdown file to Google Drive.
  2. Select the file in Drive and confirm that a formatted preview appears instead of plain text.
  3. Open the file with Google Docs to edit it or add comments while it stays a Markdown file.

Notes written in Markdown editors such as Obsidian can now be edited in Docs while keeping their original structure. Users who previously converted those notes into Google Docs format no longer need that step for new files.

Because Docs keeps the original file type, edited files remain usable in other Markdown tools after collaborators finish working on them in Google's editor. Workspace administrators cannot turn the feature off.

Accounts that do not see Markdown previews or editing yet should receive them within the 15-day rollout window, and Google's Help Center page "View and edit Markdown (.md) files in Google Docs" lists further details.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Google Docs Adds Native Markdown File Editing, With Rendered .md Previews in Google Drive appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Rockstar Says GTA 6 Avoids Satire Aimed at Specific Real People, Events, or Movements (2026)
item.description:
Rockstar Games does not want Grand Theft Auto 6 to be too specific about any real person, event, or political movement, according to Rupert Humphries, the studio's senior vice president of narrative.

Humphries made the comments in a new interview with Love magazine, about six weeks before GTA 6 launches on PS5 and Xbox Series consoles on November 19, 2026.

Humphries says earlier Grand Theft Auto games never put much focus on national politics. He points to GTA 4 as the closest example, where Homeland Security and the Patriot Act were central themes because post-9/11 New York was a frontline for those issues.

How GTA 6 Handles Politics and Satire in Leonida

Rockstar tries to make games that feel tied to the moment they release without mirroring the exact world players live in, Humphries explains. Satire built around a particular person or news event works against that goal.

The studio focuses on Florida itself instead. According to Humphries, Rockstar filled Leonida, its fictional version of the state, with characters and culture wars meant to make the world feel alive, drawing on the locals, police officers, and gang members the team met during research trips to Florida. Satire stays larger than life and runs through original characters and scenarios rather than real ones. Political themes reach players indirectly through:

  • election signs placed around the game world
  • robocalls from political campaigns
  • commercials on in-game radio stations
  • political talk shows on the radio that discuss current issues

Humphries also describes the American Dream as a recurring theme of the series. GTA 4 told an immigrant's story as commentary on the illusion of America as a land of opportunity, and GTA 5 pushed that cynicism further, he says.

Rockstar on Jason's Army Backstory

The interview also covered Jason, one of the two GTA 6 protagonists. Rockstar's official character description says Jason grew up around grifters and crooks and spent time in the Army before returning to work for local drug runners.

Humphries says Rockstar "didn't want to make any kind of statement" with that history. Jason turns to drug trafficking and bank robbery because of his material circumstances, he explains, but players can decide for themselves whether Jason needs to do it or is simply wired differently from other people.

GTA 6 follows Jason and Lucia across Leonida, and content details have also come from ratings boards, such as PEGI's 18 rating for GTA 6. The interview gives no release details beyond the confirmed November 19 date and console platforms.

Rockstar has not said how large a role Jason's military past plays in the story, and Humphries did not name any specific political topics the game covers.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Rockstar Says GTA 6 Avoids Satire Aimed at Specific Real People, Events, or Movements appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Microsoft Will Block .msix and .msixbundle Attachments in New Outlook and Outlook on the Web in November (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft will block .msix and .msixbundle file attachments by default in new Outlook for Windows and Outlook on the web, according to a Microsoft 365 Message Center post (MC1488841). The change applies to Exchange Online, and the rollout is scheduled for early to mid-November 2026.

Once the block is active, users of the two affected Outlook clients will no longer be able to download or open attachments with either extension. The .msix format is used for Windows application packages, and .msixbundle files hold bundles of those packages.

Microsoft describes both file types as "infrequently used" in email. The company says the update is part of its ongoing work to strengthen security and protect organizations from unsafe file attachments.

Why Microsoft Is Adding MSIX Packages to the Outlook Block List

A malicious .msix package that a user installs without checking can compromise a Windows device. Microsoft has dealt with abuse of its app packaging system before. In December 2023, the company disabled the ms-appinstaller protocol handler by default after attackers used it to distribute malware.

The attachment block adds another layer of protection on top of that change. Outlook on the web already blocks other file types that can run code, including .py Python files, .ps1 PowerShell scripts, and .cab files.

item.title: Google Prepares to Remove the "Only Send SMS and MMS Messages" Toggle From Google Messages (2026)
item.description:
Google is preparing to remove the "Only send SMS and MMS messages" setting from Google Messages on Android, according to code strings found in the beta version messages.android_20261002_00_RC00 of the app. The change is not live in the stable release, and Google has not announced it.

The toggle currently sits in the conversation details screen. Turning it on forces Google Messages to use SMS and MMS instead of RCS for that one conversation, while RCS stays active for every other contact.

Without the toggle, the choice becomes all or nothing. Users will either disable RCS entirely in Google Messages or keep it turned on for every contact.

Google Messages Will Show a Banner Before the Setting Disappears

The beta code contains the text for a banner on the home screen of the app. Titled "Switch to RCS chats now," the banner tells users that the "Only send SMS & MMS messages" setting is going away and asks them to switch now or let it update automatically. It offers two buttons, Switch now and Dismiss.

Those strings point to a gradual migration rather than a silent removal. Conversations that use the SMS-only setting would move to RCS when the user taps Switch now, or later when the app updates them on its own. Ignoring the banner does not delete any chats, and the strings do not mention a deadline for the automatic switch.

The per-conversation toggle has practical value for some users. People rely on it to keep specific contacts on SMS, and it has also served as a way to limit spam in Google Messages. The removal is one of a string of changes to the app, which recently added a floating long-press menu and swipe gestures.

How to Check Which Google Messages Chats Use SMS Only

Users who depend on the setting can review their conversations before the banner arrives:

  1. Open Google Messages and select a conversation.
  2. Open the conversation details screen.
  3. Check whether the "Only send SMS and MMS messages" toggle is turned on, and note the contacts that use it.

After the toggle is gone, the only remaining way to avoid RCS for a contact will be to turn off RCS for all conversations in the Google Messages settings.

The code strings do not include a date, and Google has not confirmed when the setting will be removed from the stable version of Google Messages.

item.title: Google Releases Chrome 155 With 247 Security Fixes, Four of Them Rated Critical (2026)
item.description:
Google has released Chrome 155 to the Stable channel with 247 security fixes, according to the Chrome Releases blog. The desktop update, version 155.0.8059.39/.40 for Windows and Mac and 155.0.8059.39 for Linux, will roll out over the coming days and weeks.

Four of the 247 fixes are rated Critical. Google lists 53 more as High severity, 122 as Medium, and 68 as Low. That count is far above recent Chrome security updates: the October 1 desktop update to version 154.0.8037.97 contained 11 fixes.

Chrome 155 is also out on Android as version 155.0.8059.39, reaching Google Play over the next few days, and on iOS as version 155.0.8059.37 through the App Store.

Google says Android releases contain the same security fixes as the corresponding desktop build unless otherwise noted. The new version arrives a week after Chrome 154.0.8037.92, which shipped with 32 security fixes on September 29.

Critical Chrome 155 Vulnerabilities and Who Reported Them

All four critical issues are use after free bugs. Google lists them in these components:

  • Chromecast (CVE-2026-106382), reported by Google
  • Browser (CVE-2026-106197), reported by Xinyang Ge
  • Navigation (CVE-2026-106358), reported by Xinyang Ge of Anthropic, assisted by Claude
  • Track (CVE-2026-106347), reported by Xinyang Ge of Anthropic, assisted by Claude

Among the high severity entries, Google lists a $5,000 bounty for an incorrect authorization issue in Site Isolation (CVE-2026-102322), while bounties for the critical bugs are listed as not applicable or still to be decided. Other high severity fixes cover the ANGLE graphics layer, Autofill, the Omnibox, the Translate feature, and Chrome for iOS.

Google keeps bug details and links restricted until a majority of users are updated with a fix. Restrictions stay in place longer when a bug sits in a third party library that other projects also depend on and have not yet fixed.

Chrome 155 reached the Stable channel in two steps. Google first pushed version 155.0.8059.26/.27 to a small percentage of Windows and Mac users on September 30 as an early stable release, before the wider rollout on October 6. Chrome 156 entered the Beta channel on September 30, and the Dev channel is already on version 157.

How to Update Chrome to Version 155

Because the rollout is gradual, some desktop installations will not receive Chrome 155 right away. Users can check for the update manually:

  1. Open the Chrome menu and select Help, then About Google Chrome.
  2. Wait for Chrome to check for and download version 155.
  3. Click Relaunch to finish installing the update.

On the same day, Google moved the Extended Stable channel to version 152.0.7977.158 for Windows and Mac. The Chrome Releases blog does not say whether any of the 247 vulnerabilities fixed in Chrome 155 have been exploited, and details of the four critical bugs remain restricted for now.

item.title: Microsoft Says GTA 6 Will Not Stream Exclusively on Xbox or Be Playable on PC Through the Cloud (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft has denied that Xbox holds exclusive cloud streaming rights to GTA 6 and says the game will not stream to PC at launch. Xbox Chief Strategy Officer Matthew Ball made the statement in a post on X, after reports claimed that Xbox Cloud Gaming would be the only place to stream the game when it releases in November.

"While the excitement for GTA VI and Xbox is great to see, it has also led to some misreporting," Ball wrote. "We are looking forward to launching GTA VI on Xbox November 19, though the game will not be streaming exclusively or to PC."

What the GTA 6 Streaming Reports Claimed

According to the reports, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma told employees at a recent internal town hall that the company had something planned for GTA 6 that "no other platform holder is doing." Sources identified that plan as exclusive streaming rights for the game, starting with its November launch.

The claim drew attention because of what it implied for PC players. Xbox Cloud Gaming runs on PCs, smart TVs, and mobile devices, so an Xbox streaming deal would have let players without a console run GTA 6 on a PC before Rockstar releases a native port. Rockstar has not announced a PC version, and the game launches on consoles only.

Ball's statement rules out both parts of the report. Xbox does not have exclusive streaming rights, and the Xbox Cloud Gaming app on PC will not offer GTA 6. The wording leaves open streaming on other devices, but Microsoft has not specified which ones will support the game.

Xbox Cloud Gaming Hour Limits Start the Same Month

November also brings new monthly limits to Xbox Cloud Gaming. Xbox Game Pass Ultimate subscribers will get 15 hours of streaming, with more hours available for purchase, and pay-as-you-go plans are scheduled to arrive the same month.

Those plans would let players without a console pay for timed access to streamed games, although Ball's statement means a PC will not be one of the ways to stream GTA 6.

Sony holds the marketing rights to GTA 6. PlayStation is selling limited-edition GTA 6 DualSense controllers, and Rockstar promotes the game with branding that says it "plays best" on PS5. Xbox, for its part, says its share of GTA 6 pre-orders matches its share of the console market.

For Xbox console owners, the plan has not changed. GTA 6 still launches on Xbox on November 19, the same date Rockstar used when it confirmed GTA 6 hurricanes and six map regions.

Players who hoped to stream the game on a PC through Xbox Cloud Gaming will need a console at launch, and Rockstar has not publicly commented on the streaming reports.

item.title: Microsoft Tests a New Windows 11 Search That Can Toggle Settings and Snap Windows From the Taskbar (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft has started rolling out a redesigned Windows Search experience to Windows Insiders that can carry out actions, such as switching to dark mode or snapping windows, directly from the search box on the taskbar in Windows 11.

The company announced the change in a Windows Insider Blog post on October 7, 2026, and says the rollout is gradual and limited to the Experimental channel for now.

The new search is rebuilt on WinUI 3, which Microsoft says makes it faster and more efficient with system resources. It also drops the familiar layout with a results list on the left and a preview pane on the right. A single list now groups all results together, a decision Microsoft explains by noting that most clicks in Windows Search come from that left-hand list anyway.

Windows Search Adds Inline Actions for Settings and Windows

Inline actions are the main addition. Instead of returning a link to a Settings page, the new search executes a request typed in plain language. Microsoft lists these examples in the announcement:

  • toggling settings with requests like "switch to dark mode," "turn on night light," or "turn on Bluetooth"
  • making quick adjustments such as "dim my screen" or "mute"
  • managing windows by minimizing all open windows or arranging and snapping them
  • sending a text through a phone connected with Phone Link, which Microsoft says is coming soon

Search is also getting better at handling typos and synonyms. Microsoft plans to keep tuning that behavior over the coming weeks.

More is planned for later in 2026: inline previews of documents and photos with richer file details, inline web answers for queries such as weather, stock prices, or the height of a landmark, and filters for categories like files. In 2027, Microsoft intends to bring the experience to the Start menu and adapt it to different taskbar positions and configurations.

Searches started from Start keep the current experience during the early previews. Copilot integration is mentioned only as a direction, without any details.

How Windows Insiders Can Enable the New Search

The redesigned search requires build 26340.9616 in the Experimental channel or build 28120.3181 in the Experimental 26H1 channel, and it supports English only in this first release. Insiders on a qualifying build turn it on with a feature flag:

  1. Install the qualifying build, open Settings > Windows Update, select Check for updates, and restart the PC.
  2. Go to Settings > Windows Update > Windows Insider Program > Feature flags.
  3. Enable the "New Windows Search Experience" flag.

The flag only appears after the update check and restart, according to Microsoft. Feedback goes through Feedback Hub (Win + F) under Desktop Environment > Search.

The announcement does not say whether queries and actions are processed locally or in the cloud, and it lists no privacy details or hardware requirements. Microsoft has also not given a date for the new search to reach stable versions of Windows 11.

item.title: Google Rolls Out Pixel Buds Firmware 6.144 With Dynamic ANC and a Tap-to-Mute Gesture (2026)
item.description:
Google has started rolling out a firmware update for the Pixel Buds Pro, Pixel Buds Pro 2, and Pixel Buds 2a that brings Dynamic Active Noise Cancellation to the Pixel Buds Pro 2, a tap gesture to mute calls, and automatic pausing when the wearer falls asleep. The update carries firmware version release_6.144 and arrives through the Pixel Buds app on Android.

The release follows a feature Google began rolling out last month that lets Pixel Buds owners change earbud settings by asking Gemini. That integration goes beyond volume control and covers adjusting the EQ, turning ANC on or off, and changing other Pixel Buds settings by voice.

Pixel Buds Update Brings Dynamic ANC, Tap to Mute, and Sleep Detection

Dynamic ANC is the headline addition for the Pixel Buds Pro 2. Google has previously explained that the feature adjusts noise cancellation automatically based on the seal of the earbuds in the ear.

If an earbud shifts slightly and the seal changes, the earbuds compensate and adjust ANC to match. The feature is now starting to reach Pixel Buds Pro 2 owners.

The update also includes these changes:

  • a tap-to-mute and unmute gesture for phone calls and online meetings, triggered by tapping the surface of the earbuds
  • automatic pausing of media playback when the wearer falls asleep, which also disables touch gestures and silences notifications
  • an enhanced Live Translate mode that starts translating with a gesture on the earbuds, so the phone can stay in a pocket

Sleep detection comes with a hardware dependency. The earbuds rely on a paired Pixel Watch to detect when the wearer has fallen asleep, so owners without the watch will not get that feature. For translation, Google says the earbuds now work more seamlessly with the Google Translate app.

The update lands during Amazon's October sale, where the Pixel Buds Pro 2 are discounted from $229 to about $170. That is a retailer promotion, not a permanent price change from Google.

How to Check for the Pixel Buds Firmware Update

The rollout is gradual, so not every pair will show the update right away. Owners can check manually:

  1. Update the Pixel Buds app to the latest version.
  2. Connect the earbuds and open More Settings > Firmware.
  3. Select Check for updates and confirm that the installed firmware is release_6.144.

Dynamic ANC is listed for the Pixel Buds Pro 2 only. Google has not detailed which of the other new features apply to each of the three supported models, so Pixel Buds Pro and Pixel Buds 2a owners should check the feature list in the app after installing the update.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Google Rolls Out Pixel Buds Firmware 6.144 With Dynamic ANC and a Tap-to-Mute Gesture appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Rockstar Says GTA 6 Will Require Players to Earn Money to Advance Story Missions (2026)
item.description:
Rockstar Games North co-studio head Rob Nelson says Grand Theft Auto 6 will require players to earn money in the open world at certain points before the story can continue. Nelson made the comments in an interview recorded earlier this year and published in full this week, with GTA 6 scheduled to launch next month.

"We have made money matter more in this story than I think it has in previous GTA games," Nelson said. He explained that there will be times when players have to go out into the world and make money, whether by boosting cars and selling them or by sticking places up, in order to advance the mission flow.

GTA 6 Ties Story Progress to In-Game Cash

The statement means cash is part of mission progression in GTA 6, not only a resource for buying weapons, vehicles, or property. A player who reaches one of these points without enough money will have to stop and earn it before the next mission becomes available.

Nelson named two ways to raise the money: stealing cars to sell them and robbing locations. Both fit the story of protagonists Jason and Lucia, whose finances look set to play a direct role in the narrative.

Players planning a story-focused first playthrough should expect to spend some time on these money-making activities between missions. Rockstar has not said how much cash individual missions require, how often these checkpoints appear, or whether other income sources count toward them.

Rockstar Addresses Sex Scenes and Intimacy in GTA 6

In the same interview, Nelson addressed how GTA 6 handles physical intimacy between Jason and Lucia. Nelson described intimacy as a central part of any relationship and said it "has to be done right," adding that the team keeps iterating on those scenes until they feel right. "We definitely want to err on the right side of it," Nelson said.

When the interviewer suggested that certain minigames should not show up in the game, Nelson laughed and agreed. He did not name it, but the exchange recalls Hot Coffee in GTA: San Andreas, a scrapped sex minigame that was never meant to be playable yet was datamined from the game files and later unlocked by modders.

GTA 6 does include sexual content. The game's European age rating, covered in the PEGI 18 rating for GTA 6, lists scenes of intercourse and occasional scenes of sexual fetishes.

Rockstar has not shown how these scenes are presented in the final game, and the studio has not released further details on the money requirements ahead of launch.

item.title: Microsoft Teams Will Add Third-Party Deepfake Detection and Impersonation Warnings to Meetings in November (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft is preparing to add support for third-party deepfake detection tools and a new impersonation protection feature to Microsoft Teams meetings, according to two new entries on the Microsoft 365 Roadmap. Both features are listed as in development, and Microsoft plans to reach general availability in November after a worldwide rollout.

The deepfake detection itself will not come from Microsoft. Teams acts as the surface for detection signals sent by certified third-party providers, while the separate impersonation protection feature is built into Teams and flags suspicious meeting organizers and participants.

How Deepfake Detection Signals Work in Teams Meetings

According to the roadmap entry, organizations will be able to "enhance meeting security with synthetic audio and video detection solutions provided by certified third-party providers."

Those providers analyze the audio and video of a meeting for signs of synthetic or manipulated media. When a solution finds something, it sends a detection signal to Teams.

Microsoft says it will provide the Teams integration and the in-meeting experiences and controls that surface those signals and let organizations act on them. The roadmap entries do not name the certified providers, and Microsoft has not said whether the integration requires an additional license.

Impersonation protection targets identity rather than media. "When Teams detects a potential impersonation attempt, it surfaces warnings and risk indicators to help users recognize suspicious identities and make more informed decisions when joining or participating in a meeting," Microsoft states in the second roadmap entry.

Why Microsoft Keeps Adding Protection to Teams

The two features continue a series of Teams security changes. Cybercrime groups, ransomware gangs among them, have abused Teams for social engineering attacks aimed at the employees of victim organizations, in some cases by posing as IT support.

Microsoft has answered with a run of smaller controls:

  • admins can lock out external users through the Defender portal, a change Microsoft announced in December with availability from January
  • a meeting protection policy, rolling out since August, automatically blocks identified external bots from joining meetings
  • Teams blurs QR codes sent by external senders to cut down on phishing and fraud attempts
  • Users will be able to report suspicious guest invitations directly from Teams starting in November

The changes fit a wider tightening across Microsoft 365, which also includes blocking .msix attachments in new Outlook from November.

Teams administrators who plan to use deepfake detection should track the two roadmap entries and check which certified providers become available once the rollout starts. Organizations that already work with a synthetic media detection vendor can ask whether that vendor is pursuing certification for Teams.

Microsoft has not published a specific November date for either feature, and the roadmap entries do not explain how admins will turn them on.

item.title: Google Ends Safety Signal on Pixel Watch 2 and Pixel Watch 3 LTE Models on December 12 (2026)
item.description:
Google will end Safety Signal on the Pixel Watch 2 and Pixel Watch 3 LTE models on December 12, 2026, according to an announcement the company posted in the Google Pixel Watch Help Community. After that date, the watches lose the always-on connection that let their emergency features work without a cellular plan.

Safety Signal gave the LTE versions of both watches a connection for emergency tools even when no carrier plan was active. Google says it will notify affected owners by email and with a push notification on the watch before the service ends.

Which Pixel Watch Features Depend on Safety Signal

On the Pixel Watch 2 and Pixel Watch 3 LTE models, Safety Signal supplied the connection for these personal safety tools:

  • calling emergency contacts from the watch
  • Safety Check
  • Emergency Sharing
  • Emergency SOS
  • Fall Detection

Access was tied to a subscription to Google's Health Premium service, with Google covering the connectivity instead of a mobile carrier.

Google is not removing any of these features from the watches. What disappears on December 12 is the connectivity Safety Signal provided. The emergency tools keep working as long as the watch has its own connection, either through a cellular plan or by staying connected to a paired phone.

References to the shutdown had already turned up in code before the announcement. The December 12 end date is now official.

What Pixel Watch 2 and Pixel Watch 3 Owners Should Do

Owners who relied on Safety Signal to reach help without a phone nearby have about two months to pick a replacement:

  1. Decide whether the watch can stay tethered to a paired phone. Emergency features keep working through that connection, and it is the cheaper option for most owners.
  2. If the watch needs to work on its own, compare cellular plans for it. Google lists supported carriers on its Pixel Watch help page about mobile network providers.
  3. Look out for the email and the on-watch notification from Google, which confirm the change for the affected device.

A separate cellular plan for the watch comes with a monthly carrier fee, which makes tethering the default choice for owners who usually carry their phone.

Newer hardware offers a different route. The Pixel Watch 4 and Pixel Watch 5 support satellite connectivity, which lets wearers notify emergency contacts and emergency services when no traditional network signal is available. The wearer starts the connection and positions the watch until it locks on to a satellite.

Google has not commented beyond the announcement, including on whether Health Premium pricing changes for Pixel Watch 2 and Pixel Watch 3 LTE owners after Safety Signal ends.

item.title: UK ICO Secures Data Protection Commitments From OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Seven Other AI Developers (2026)
item.description:
The UK data protection regulator, the ICO, says ten of the largest AI developers, including OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft, have changed how they handle personal data or committed to doing so after it examined their compliance with UK data protection law. The ICO announced the outcome on Thursday, October 8, and said its next focus is autonomous AI agents.

The ten companies named by the regulator are Amazon, Anthropic, Apple, Cohere, DeepSeek, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Stability AI.

What the AI Developers Agreed to Change

According to the ICO, the commitments cover three areas:

  • clearer explanations of how personal information is used to train AI models
  • better ways for people to exercise their data rights
  • tougher assessments of the safeguards developers have in place

The changes come out of a supervisory program the ICO launched in 2025. That program initially covered 11 developers. The count dropped to ten after the regulator paused its engagement with Elon Musk's xAI to pursue a separate formal investigation into the Grok chatbot.

Richard Nevinson, the ICO's director of technology regulation, said the benefits of AI depend on trust and transparency, and that the engagement "has secured real commitments that will help people better understand and control how their data is used."

The ICO is not treating the matter as closed. The regulator says it is monitoring whether developers deliver on the promises, and it admits that current AI training practices still raise problems under UK data protection law.

Open questions include personal data held inside trained models (sensitive information in particular), how people can get their details removed once a model has been trained on them, and the risk of personal information being extracted from models. Some of these issues, the ICO says, will need cooperation between industry, regulators, and government.

ICO Opens a Call for Evidence on AI Agents

The regulator has contacted OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and the UK's AI Security Institute following reports of AI agents bypassing safeguards during testing and deployment earlier this year. "Our message is clear: the fact AI agents act with autonomy is not an excuse for poor compliance," Nevinson said.

A six-week call for evidence on agentic AI is now open. It covers security, transparency, accountability, and the lawful use of personal data, and responses are due by November 20. The ICO says the input will inform future guidance and its forthcoming statutory code of practice on AI and automated decision-making.

For UK users of services from the ten developers, the practical change is on the transparency side: clearer training explanations and easier rights requests are part of the commitments, so it is worth checking each provider's privacy information and data controls as updates appear. AI companies have recently been adding new data choices of their own, such as Anthropic's opt-in setting for voice recordings.

The ICO is also examining separately how consumer chatbots and AI companions use personal information. The regulator has not set a date for reporting on whether the ten developers have delivered on their commitments.

item.title: Rockstar Reveals Six GTA 6 Radio Stations and the Series' First In-Game Podcasts (2026)
item.description:
Rockstar Games has revealed six in-game radio stations for GTA 6 and confirmed that Grand Theft Auto VI is the first game in the series with on-demand podcasts, according to a Rockstar Newswire announcement published on October 8. The studio also opened a music page on its website where players can preview each of the six stations in two-minute samples.

Rockstar says GTA 6 will have the "biggest and widest-ranging selection of in-game radio yet." The six stations are only part of the lineup, since the announcement also confirms classic rock and talk radio options.

GTA 6 Radio Stations, Hosts, and Songs Revealed So Far

Every station revealed so far has two hosts, and Rockstar cast well-known artists in most of the roles:

  • The modern Latin station is hosted by El Martillo (voiced by Bad Bunny) and La Gata (voiced by RaiNao), covering bachata, merengue, dembow, and reggaeton, with Bad Bunny's EoO in the selection.
  • Back Country Radio plays renegade country with MW (voiced by Morgan Wallen) and Delta Dawne (voiced by Lana Del Rey), plus roving reporter Mud Dog Mike (voiced by Jeremy Dufrene). Loretta Lynn and David Allan Coe are on the playlist.
  • AfroBank FM features Burna (voiced by Burna Boy) and Palmsy (voiced by Palms Trax), with African music ranging from 20th century classics to amapiano and 3-step.
  • The Chamber 106.6 is the classic metal station, hosted by DJ Kerry (voiced by Kerry King) and DJ Tom (voiced by Tom Araya), with Black Sabbath, Pantera, and Slayer.
  • Flash FM returns as the Vice City pop station with Robyn and Alex Consani, playing Charli xcx, MGMT, and Zara Larsson with PinkPantheress.
  • Dirty South Classics covers regional rap and hip-hop with Trick Daddy and Trina, including tracks from David Banner, JT Money, and DJ Khaled.

Radio and Podcasts Now Play on Foot in GTA 6

The podcasts are the larger structural change. "For the first time ever, Grand Theft Auto VI introduces a series of on-demand podcasts for Jason and Lucia to experience beyond Leonida's terrestrial radio," Rockstar states. Both radio and podcasts can be played in vehicles and on foot, through new headphones and earbuds connected to the characters' smartphones.

In earlier Grand Theft Auto games, radio was confined to vehicles and select buildings. With the on-foot option, players can keep music or a podcast running while exploring or during combat.

Rockstar released a batch of new official screenshots alongside the radio reveal. In September, the studio confirmed a separate album of original music made for GTA 6, with songs from Travis Scott, Morgan Wallen, and Keith Richards, and the full tracklist for that album has not been published yet. The radio news follows Rockstar's recent statement that GTA 6 requires players to earn money to advance story missions.

The six station previews are available on the Rockstar Games website now. GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, and Rockstar has not said whether it will reveal the complete station list before release.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Rockstar Reveals Six GTA 6 Radio Stations and the Series' First In-Game Podcasts appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Microsoft Replaces 1TB per Person With a Shared 2TB OneDrive Pool in Microsoft 365 Family and Premium (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft is changing how OneDrive cloud storage works in Microsoft 365 Family and Premium, replacing the 1 TB that each member received with a single 2 TB pool shared by up to six people, according to an updated Microsoft support document.

New and upgraded subscriptions use the shared model starting October 8, 2026. Existing subscribers move over at their first renewal on or after May 2, 2027.

A fully used Family plan previously offered up to 6 TB in total, at 1 TB per person. The new allocation is 2 TB for the entire subscription, with no change in price.

Microsoft 365 Pro includes 5 TB of shared storage, while Microsoft 365 Basic (100 GB) and Microsoft 365 Personal (1 TB) remain single-user plans and are unaffected.

How Microsoft 365 Shared Storage Works

The primary subscriber and up to five additional members draw from the same pool. Storage add-ons purchased by any member go into that pool, and eligible family members' free storage grants count toward it too. Files stay private, so each member sees only their own content unless they share it.

Microsoft's FAQ asks whether the change is a reduction in storage and answers that "total storage varies by plan," before pointing to flexibility. A subscription owner who does not share the plan can use the full 2 TB, which is double the previous per-person amount. Households with heavy users are in a different position. Four members storing 700 GB each would total 2.8 TB, which is 800 GB over the new limit.

Subscriptions that go over 2 TB do not lose access immediately. Microsoft says members receive notifications as the plan approaches the limit and can keep accessing their files for up to one year while they manage their storage.

Extra storage can be purchased up to a total of 10 TB per subscription. Some existing Family and Premium subscribers in supported markets may receive bonus storage at renewal at no extra cost, but Microsoft has not published amounts or durations.

What Existing Family and Premium Subscribers Should Check

Nothing changes for existing plans before May 2, 2027, and Microsoft says it will email subscribers before the renewal that triggers the switch. One rule matters right now: upgrading moves a subscription to shared storage immediately.

Switching from Family to Premium before May 2, 2027 applies the 2 TB pool at once, while a downgrade alone does not trigger the change.

  1. Have each member open the storage dashboard in their Microsoft account and note how much OneDrive space they use.
  2. Add the numbers together and compare the total with the 2 TB limit.
  3. Note the subscription renewal date, since the switch happens at the first renewal on or after May 2, 2027.
  4. Hold off on upgrading from Family to Premium if the household stores more than 2 TB combined.
  5. Free up space by deleting duplicate photo backups and emptying the OneDrive recycle bin, which counts against the quota.

Microsoft has not said what happens to files that remain over the limit once the one-year grace period ends.

item.title: Tesla Renames Full Self-Driving to Tesla Assisted Driving in Europe After German Regulator Talks (2026)
item.description:
Tesla has renamed its Full Self-Driving (Supervised) driver-assistance feature to Tesla Assisted Driving (TAD) in Europe, according to a statement from the German Transport Ministry.

Tesla offered the name change after talks with the ministry last month, and on Friday the automaker started using the Tesla Assisted Driving name on its European sales website.

The ministry says German Transport Minister Steffen Bilger found the "FSD" name "somewhat misleading." Following the discussions with Tesla, Bilger said he would now advocate for European regulators to approve the feature "as quickly as possible." A vote on approval at EU level is expected by the end of the year.

Tesla Assisted Driving Approval Status in Europe

The rename does not change what the software does. Tesla Assisted Driving can accelerate, brake, steer, and park the car, but Tesla requires drivers to stay alert and ready to intervene at all times. The feature cannot drive the vehicle on its own.

Europe is still mostly closed to the system. The Netherlands became the first European government to give Tesla provisional permission to launch it this past spring.

Australia and New Zealand approved the feature last year, and a version became available to customers in China in May. In the US, Tesla charges $99 per month for a Full Self-Driving (Supervised) subscription. European pricing for Tesla Assisted Driving has not been announced.

Why Regulators Pushed Back on the Full Self-Driving Name

Tesla resisted changing the name for years and defended it in court. Last year, California's Department of Motor Vehicles concluded that Tesla's use of the terms "Full Self-Driving" and "Autopilot" was misleading and violated state law.

After the agency threatened to suspend Tesla's manufacturing and dealer licenses in California, the automaker stopped using "Autopilot," an older and less capable driver-assistance feature. Tesla also kept "(Supervised)" attached to the official Full Self-Driving name.

The software remains under scrutiny in the US. In March, the federal government opened a probe into Full Self-Driving after nine incidents in which the system allegedly failed to respond in reduced visibility and did not warn drivers to take over. Tesla recalled an older version of the software in 2023 after US authorities found that it did not follow some traffic laws.

Tesla and CEO Elon Musk have pushed for years to get the driver-assistance technology approved in other global markets.

For Tesla owners and buyers in Europe, the practical effect is limited. The new name applies to marketing and sales material, and outside of the Dutch provisional permission, the feature still lacks approval for use on public roads. Owners should continue to treat the system as driver assistance that requires constant supervision, which is what Tesla's own requirements state.

Tesla did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the rename, and the EU has not set a firm date for its approval vote.

item.title: GTA 6 Leaker Threatens to Release a Full Story Mode Build Unless Take-Two Offers Physical Discs (2026)
item.description:
The GTA 6 leaker known as Cyberleek has threatened to release a build of the game containing the full story mode, "played to the end, credits and all," if the leaker's memecoin reaches a market cap of $30 million.

The warning appeared on the Cyberleek website, which demands that Take-Two Interactive release GTA 6 on physical discs and issue a public apology to stop the leak.

Cyberleek's statement says Take-Two "gets one way out: physical disks and a public apology." The leaker frames the GTA 6 leaks as a protest against the lack of a disc version of the game. It is unclear whether Cyberleek intends to publish a playable build online or a full playthrough in video form.

How the Cyberleek Memecoin Threat Works

The memecoin's market cap stood at $3.8 million when the threat was reported, after spiking to $5.7 million as news of the message spread on social media. Reaching $30 million would require roughly an eightfold increase.

The website also lists lower thresholds tied to further leaked gameplay footage. At $2 million and $4 million, Cyberleek promised clips showing co-protagonist Lucia in increasingly revealing states of undress. A poll where fans pay to vote on the next leak using the leaker's cryptocurrency is reportedly live on the site.

Fans are skeptical of the physical media argument, and the leaker has been widely accused of running a cryptocurrency scam. Analysis of crypto transactions in late August pointed to Cyberleek having cashed out around $270,000. Every video the leaker has posted links to the same website and coin.

Take-Two Investigation and Rockstar's Response

Cyberleek went quiet after a series of GTA 6 leaks in August that led Take-Two to open an investigation, including subpoenas to Discord and other services in federal court. The leaker returned this week with a 24-minute gameplay video showing cutscenes, story beats, a first-person camera, and nude scenes of Jason and Lucia. An earlier clip ended with the word "LEEK" shot into a wall, which indicates access to a playable build.

How the footage, or any build behind it, left Rockstar's development environment is still unknown. In August, Rockstar called the leaks "heartbreaking" for its development team and "unfortunate" for fans.

The studio acknowledged that the intended experience "may now be impacted by some spoilers" and kept the November 19 release date unchanged, the same date Rockstar confirmed ahead of the console launch.

For players, two points follow from the facts so far. Buying the Cyberleek coin funds the leaker directly and carries the usual risks of an unregulated memecoin with no official link to Rockstar or Take-Two.

Players who want to avoid story spoilers before release should also expect more unofficial footage to circulate on social media and video sites in the weeks before launch.

Rockstar and Take-Two have not commented on the latest threat, and there is no confirmation that the leaked material contains the complete story mode.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post GTA 6 Leaker Threatens to Release a Full Story Mode Build Unless Take-Two Offers Physical Discs appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Microsoft Retires Themes by Copilot in Outlook Starting in Mid-October (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft is retiring Themes by Copilot in Outlook worldwide, with the removal starting in mid-October 2026 and expected to finish by late October 2026, according to the Microsoft 365 Message Center post MC1492954, published on October 9.

The change applies to users with a Copilot license on new Outlook for Windows, Outlook for Android, Outlook for iOS, Outlook for Mac, and Outlook on the web.

Once the retirement reaches an account, Themes by Copilot is removed from Outlook's settings. Copilot themes can no longer be selected, and anyone who switches to a different theme cannot go back to a Copilot one afterward.

Microsoft gives no reason for the retirement in the message. Outlook users without a Copilot license are not affected by the change.

What Happens to Existing Copilot Themes in Outlook

A Copilot theme that is already applied stays in place until the user changes it. Themes set to refresh automatically also remain applied, but they stop refreshing and keep the imagery they show at the moment of the retirement.

Themes by Copilot was offered to Copilot Pro and Microsoft 365 Copilot subscribers in the Appearance settings of Outlook. Users could start from a weather type or a location, either their own or one of more than 100 curated destinations, and then choose a realistic, oil painting, or cartoon art style.

Each generated theme combined a wallpaper, shown as the background on desktop or at the top of the mobile apps, with a matching accent color for the rest of the interface. Refresh intervals ranged from every few hours to daily, weekly, or monthly.

Microsoft launched a separate collection of standard themes, which are not AI-generated, for all Outlook users regardless of license status, with color options such as green, red, and purple. The retirement notice covers only Themes by Copilot.

What Copilot License Holders Should Check in Outlook

The Message Center post states that no action is required. Users who like their current Copilot wallpaper should still keep the following in mind before the removal arrives:

  1. Leave the current Copilot theme applied if the imagery should stay, since switching to any other theme removes the option to return.
  2. Expect auto-refreshing Copilot themes to freeze on their current image once the retirement reaches the account.
  3. Pick a replacement from the standard theme collection in Outlook's Appearance settings if a frozen image is not wanted.

The removal comes shortly after Microsoft announced plans to block .msix attachments in new Outlook in November.

Microsoft is rolling the retirement out gradually across the mid to late October window, so Themes by Copilot remains visible in Settings on some accounts until the removal reaches them.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Microsoft Retires Themes by Copilot in Outlook Starting in Mid-October 2026 appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: WhatsApp Blocks Logins on Android and iOS Devices Running Outdated Operating Systems (2026)
item.description:
WhatsApp has started blocking logins on Android and iOS devices that run an outdated operating system. The check is a server-side change, so it works regardless of the installed WhatsApp version, and it is rolling out to specific accounts on both platforms. Affected users see a new screen asking them to update the device software before they can continue.

The screen cannot be skipped. Until the operating system is updated, WhatsApp does not let the account log in on that device. Because the check runs on WhatsApp's servers, installing a newer WhatsApp build alone does not clear the screen.

How the WhatsApp OS Update Requirement Works

WhatsApp's login screen tells users to open the device settings and install the latest available system update. It also explains how to check the software version currently installed, for anyone unsure which release the phone runs. Once the update is in place, WhatsApp opens normally and the login can be completed.

The reasoning is device security. Attackers look for known vulnerabilities in outdated operating systems to install malware, and malware on a phone can capture data before WhatsApp encrypts it.

End-to-end encryption protects messages, but it cannot protect content an attacker has already grabbed on the device, and every other app on that phone is exposed in the same way.

The block does not point to a flaw in WhatsApp itself. WhatsApp relies on the security guarantees of the operating system, and those guarantees weaken when the system is no longer current, so the app now refuses to proceed with a login on obsolete software.

The requirement is the latest in a series of account protections. WhatsApp recently tested a warning for people who connect through unofficial WhatsApp Web clients, after notifying around 200 users in Italy whose devices were compromised through a fake version of the app.

A Scam Alert feature detects suspicious messages on the device, and restricted chats limit certain conversations to the primary device.

What WhatsApp Users Should Do Now

Users on older phones can avoid being locked out by updating before the check reaches their account:

  1. Open the device settings and check which operating system version is currently installed.
  2. Install the latest system update the device offers.
  3. Open WhatsApp and complete the login after the update has finished.

There is no workaround inside WhatsApp. A phone that cannot install a newer operating system will keep showing the update screen, since the app offers no way to bypass it.

WhatsApp has not announced which Android or iOS versions trigger the block. Accounts that do not see the screen today can still get it later if the device software falls below WhatsApp's minimum requirement.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post WhatsApp Blocks Logins on Android and iOS Devices Running Outdated Operating Systems appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Valve's Deadlock Passes Team Fortress 2's All-Time Steam Peak With 262,145 Concurrent Players (2026)
item.description:
Valve's Deadlock reached 262,145 concurrent players on Steam, passing the all-time concurrent player peak of Team Fortress 2, which stands at 253,997, according to Steam player data tracked by SteamDB. The record came as Valve released Solomon, the latest of six new heroes added to the MOBA as part of its City Never Sleeps update.

Deadlock is still technically an invite-only test and has no public release date. Valve hands out invites generously, and invites are also shared in Discord communities, so getting into the game is not difficult for interested players.

The Team Fortress 2 figure has a caveat. Its Steam peak was set about three years ago and does not include players from the Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3 versions released as part of The Orange Box.

Deadlock City Never Sleeps Update Adds Heroes and a Rebuilt Map

The player surge follows the largest Deadlock update so far. City Never Sleeps overhauls the entire map, called the Cursed Apple, with new neutral monsters and reworked areas based on an occult version of 1950s New York:

  • Broadway, the center lane, is now a neon district with a miniature version of 1950s Times Square at its heart.
  • Greenwich has become an occult take on Central Park, with a university and an arboreal garden.
  • York turns its former walker arenas into a stock exchange and a factory ground.
  • The districts between lanes now have their own themes and creeps, from a theater district with creepy dolls to Chinatown with festival spirits and haunted cabbage pots.

Six heroes arrived with the update and were released one at a time. They include Violet, an art student; Deadman Danny, a skeletal crash test dummy and weapons salesman; Nurse Harrow; the Rat King, who has more than 100 voice lines; Baba, a reinvention of the Baba Yaga myth riding a bird-legged park bench; and Solomon, a chess-loving old man.

Solomon's weapon is a chess board. Players report that each reload recreates a different historic chess game state, depending on the number of bullets loaded onto the board. Valve also added dozens of new conversations and voice lines between existing characters.

How to Get Into the Deadlock Test

Access to the Deadlock test requires an invite on Steam. Players who want to try it can follow these steps:

  1. Ask a friend who already has Deadlock access to send an invite through Steam.
  2. Look for invites shared in Deadlock Discord communities if no friend has access.
  3. Accept the invite in Steam and install Deadlock.

Deadlock first leaked about two years ago, and activity in the test has grown since then. Valve has not announced when Deadlock will leave the invite-only phase or whether the new player peak will change its release plans.

item.title: Microsoft Sets November 10 as the Final Security Update for Windows 11 23H2 Enterprise and Education (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft has reminded organizations that Windows 11 version 23H2 Enterprise, Education, and IoT Enterprise editions will stop receiving security updates after the November 2026 security update, which ships on November 10, according to a post in the Windows Message Center. The company recommends moving eligible devices to a supported version of Windows 11 before that date.

"The November 2026 Windows security update will be the last update available for these editions," Microsoft said in the message center update. Devices that stay on these editions afterward will no longer get the monthly security updates that protect against the latest threats.

Consumer editions are already past this point. Windows 11 23H2 Home and Pro reached end of support in November 2025, so the November 10 release closes out version 23H2 for the remaining business, school, and IoT editions.

Windows 11 23H2 End of Support and the Upgrade Path to 26H2

Microsoft points customers to Windows 11 26H2, also called the Windows 11 2026 Update. Version 26H2 became generally available in September 2026 as an enablement package and is supported for consumers until October 2029.

The 26H2 update is rolling out in phases to eligible Windows 11 devices that have the "Get the latest updates as soon as they're available" setting turned on. If the update is ready for a device, Microsoft says it downloads and installs automatically, and a single restart completes the process.

Users and administrators can also check for the update manually:

  1. Open Settings and go to Windows Update.
  2. Select "Check for updates".
  3. If the device is eligible, select "Download and install Windows 11, version 26H2" and restart when prompted.

Organizations managing larger fleets can confirm the servicing dates for each edition on Microsoft's Windows lifecycle FAQ page or with the Lifecycle Policy search tool, which list the support windows for every Windows 11 feature update.

Other Windows Support Deadlines Arriving This Month

The 23H2 reminder arrives during a crowded lifecycle period. Windows 11 24H2 Home and Pro editions stop receiving updates this week, while the 24H2 Enterprise and Education editions remain under mainstream support until October 2027. Windows Server 2022 leaves mainstream support on Tuesday, October 13, and moves to extended support that runs until October 14, 2031.

Microsoft also warned last week that devices running unsupported Windows versions will stop getting security updates once the Windows Update certificates expire in 2027.

Home users still on Windows 10 have a separate option, since Microsoft extended the free Windows 10 Extended Security Updates program for home users until October 2027.

After November 10, PCs left on Windows 11 23H2 Enterprise, Education, or IoT Enterprise will run without monthly security fixes until they are moved to a supported Windows 11 release.

item.title: Google Launches the $179.99 Fitbit Edge With a Replaceable Battery, GPS, and a 1.34-Inch Screen (2026)
item.description:
Google has announced the Fitbit Edge, a $179.99 fitness tracker with a 1.34-inch display, built-in GPS, and a user-replaceable battery, a first for any Fitbit. Preorders opened on Monday, and the tracker goes on sale on October 27. The Edge works with both Android phones and iPhones through the Google Health app.

The Edge is the first display-equipped Fitbit tracker since the Charge 6 arrived in 2023. Google places it between the screenless Fitbit Air, which costs $99.99, and the Pixel Watch 5, which starts at $349.99. The new tracker is $20 more expensive than the Charge 6's regular price.

Fitbit Edge Hardware, Battery, and Tracking Features

The capsule-shaped Edge replaces the Charge 6's 1.04-inch screen with a larger 1.34-inch panel and swaps the haptic nub for a physical side button. According to Google, the tracker includes:

  • its own GPS chipset, which Google says tracks more accurately than the Charge 6
  • an altimeter that records elevation gain and loss and counts floors climbed
  • a far-field skin temperature sensor carried over from the Pixel Watch
  • electrical sensors that work with the ECG app
  • music controls for any audio playing on the connected phone

Battery life is rated at seven days, or about two days with the always-on display enabled. A full charge takes around 90 minutes, half an hour less than the Charge 6, and the Edge uses the same charger as the Fitbit Air. Repair options for the replaceable battery will vary by region.

Google also says Gemini-powered automatic activity tracking can identify up to 100 workout types, and the Edge offers more than 50 exercise modes, up from 40 on its predecessor. The same detection upgrades are coming to the Pixel Watch 5 and the Fitbit Air.

A Google Health Premium subscription adds blood pressure trend tracking without manual calibration and insulin resistance trends without a blood draw. Google representatives also said a phone can now be paired with a Fitbit Air and a Fitbit Edge at the same time, so owners can switch between the two. Pairing two Fitbits at once was not possible before.

What Charge 6 Owners Give Up With the Fitbit Edge

The Edge has no NFC hardware, which means no contactless payments through Google Wallet. Charge 6 owners who pay from the wrist should factor that in before preordering, because tap-to-pay is one feature the older tracker had and the new one drops.

Music control moves in the other direction: the Charge 6 only worked with YouTube Music, which required a subscription, while the Edge controls any playback on the phone.

Bands ship in Active, Active Sport, Performance Loop, Magnet, and Metal Links styles, and a Stephen Curry edition costs $220. Google Maps turn-by-turn directions are not available at launch and are scheduled to reach the Edge later this year.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Google Launches the $179.99 Fitbit Edge With a Replaceable Battery, GPS, and a 1.34-Inch Screen appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Norway Fines Microsoft's Xandr $9.6 Million Over Sharing Grindr Users' Sensitive Data (2026)
item.description:
Norway's Data Protection Authority, Datatilsynet, has fined Xandr, an advertising company owned by Microsoft, NOK 92 million ($9.6 million) for unlawfully processing and sharing sensitive data belonging to Grindr users in Norway.

The authority says this is the largest fine it has ever issued. Xandr, which now operates as Microsoft Advertising, has three weeks to appeal the decision.

"We issued such a high fine in this case because the breaches we identified were very serious," said Line Coll, Director General of Datatilsynet. "Thousands of users in Norway have been subjected to unlawful sharing of their sensitive data."

How Xandr Shared Grindr User Data in Ad Auctions

According to the authority's findings, Xandr ran real-time advertising auctions inside the Grindr dating app between July 2018 and April 2020. Advertisers bid for the right to show an ad to a Grindr user after receiving profiling information from Xandr, which acted as the intermediary. The data exposed through these auctions could include a user's sexual orientation, and it reached thousands of companies.

Datatilsynet found that Xandr was a joint controller with Grindr at the time. That role made Xandr responsible for how the data was used, and it should have required and obtained explicit consent from the people whose data it processed. Instead, Xandr assumed Grindr had collected valid consent and took no steps to check.

"Xandr omitted to verify that the consents from Grindr were valid, and did not do anything to ensure they had a legal basis for their own processing," Coll stated. Sensitive information about Grindr users in Norway and other countries reached advertisers without the users knowing about it or giving explicit consent.

Microsoft's Response and the 2020 Complaint Behind the Fine

A Microsoft spokesperson said the investigation and its outcome "focused on conduct that predates Microsoft's acquisition of Xandr." Legal frameworks, and the way regulators interpret and enforce them, have changed since then, according to the spokesperson, who added that Microsoft is "reviewing the decision and assessing our options."

The case goes back to a complaint filed in January 2020 by the Austrian privacy group noyb together with the Norwegian Consumer Council (Forbrukerrådet).

Noyb called the decision "a major blow to the online adtech industry" and said that profiling people's interests, habits, location, and behavior requires valid consent, which adtech firms rarely obtain in its view.

For Grindr users, the ruling covers past processing rather than a new setting or change inside the app. The decision applies to auctions run between July 2018 and April 2020, and the authority's findings concern Xandr's failure to verify consent during that period.

Microsoft has not said whether it will appeal before the three-week deadline runs out.

item.title: Epic Games Delays Its Unannounced Star Wars and Marvel Shooter and Moves It to AI-First Development (2026)
item.description:
Epic Games has delayed an unannounced Star Wars and Marvel crossover shooter indefinitely and told the team behind it to adopt an "AI first" production model built on AI tools, according to instructions given to staff last week.

The game had been planned for a March 2027 release that Epic never announced publicly. Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney addressed the change in a series of posts on X, describing a companywide shift toward AI development.

The instructions call for the team to use tools such as Anthropic's Claude, with art "generated with full AI workflows." Epic has not officially revealed the game, its title, or a new release window.

Tim Sweeney Explains Epic's AI Pivot

Sweeney said Epic is moving developers around "to retool for maximum AI acceleration." He added that "the aim isn't to do the same stuff with fewer people, but to enable everyone here to build MORE and BETTER stuff, and to bring the benefits to all teams using Unreal."

Responding to criticism that Epic is ignoring how players feel about generative AI, Sweeney wrote that "much of the room wants it to be 2016 again, but it's not." Epic's job as a provider of tools and technology to much of the industry, he argued, is to design for the present and the near future. He described himself as optimistic and called AI empowering for creators.

Asked whether Epic plans to speed up an IPO, Sweeney said the company's "more modest aim is to survive the AI revolution, help other developers do the same, and come out on the other end making better code and content faster."

The CEO also put numbers on the efficiency gains Epic is seeing. Current improvements range from about 20% in the most technical areas of Unreal Engine development to 5x in areas such as web development. By this time next year, Sweeney expects "very little will be less than 3x of January 2026 efficiency."

Epic's AI Push Follows 1,000 Layoffs in March

The shift comes after Epic laid off more than 1,000 employees in March. At the time, the company cited declining console sales, its ongoing legal disputes with Apple and Google, and difficulty delivering "consistent Fortnite magic with every season."

Sweeney also argued that the biggest change for game design will be a much shorter path from an idea to a playtest. In his view, most recent AAA failures trace back to game systems spending far too much of their development without being playtested.

Players following the project have little to act on yet, since the shooter exists only as an internal project with no store page or trailer. Epic has not announced a new release date for the Star Wars and Marvel shooter, and the company has not confirmed how much of the final game will use AI-generated art.

Responding to criticism that Epic is ignoring how players feel about generative AI, Sweeney wrote that "much of the room wants it to be 2016 again, but it's not." Epic's job as a provider of tools and technology to much of the industry, he argued, is to design for the present and the near future. He described himself as optimistic and called AI empowering for creators.

Asked whether Epic plans to speed up an IPO, Sweeney said the company's "more modest aim is to survive the AI revolution, help other developers do the same, and come out on the other end making better code and content faster."

The CEO also put numbers on the efficiency gains Epic is seeing. Current improvements range from about 20% in the most technical areas of Unreal Engine development to 5x in areas such as web development. By this time next year, Sweeney expects "very little will be less than 3x of January 2026 efficiency."

Epic's AI Push Follows 1,000 Layoffs in March

The shift comes after Epic laid off more than 1,000 employees in March. At the time, the company cited declining console sales, its ongoing legal disputes with Apple and Google, and difficulty delivering "consistent Fortnite magic with every season."

Sweeney also argued that the biggest change for game design will be a much shorter path from an idea to a playtest. In his view, most recent AAA failures trace back to game systems spending far too much of their development without being playtested.

Players following the project have little to act on yet, since the shooter exists only as an internal project with no store page or trailer. Epic has not announced a new release date for the Star Wars and Marvel shooter, and the company has not confirmed how much of the final game will use AI-generated art.
